$schema_note: The branch-protection spec for the obot workspace: one entry per ROLED branch in scripts/policy.json, naming the exact rule that branch should carry. It is a proposal until @jwildfire chooses (obot.roadmap#272); 'status' below says which. scripts/obot-protect turns this file into API calls ('apply') and reads the live state back against it ('verify'). Nothing here is applied automatically, and the obotclaw App cannot apply or even read branch protection - it has no 'administration' permission, deliberately: an agent that can remove its own guardrail does not have one.
status: PROPOSED - nothing applied. Awaiting @jwildfire's choice on the decision artifact below.

mechanism.why_not_rulesets: Rulesets add bypass actors, which this spec does not need: no rule here restricts WHO may merge, so obotclaw[bot] needs no exemption. Classic protection is also the mechanism already proven against the bot on safety.viz/main and gsm.safety/main since 2026-07 - every release merge on those branches went through it as obotclaw[bot]. Push restrictions ('restrictions') are organization-only and are left null on these user-owned repositories.
mechanism.credential: @jwildfire's own gh auth. Reading or writing protection needs repository admin; the obotclaw App has neither and must not be given them.

history-guard._summary: Force-push and deletion are refused; everything else is unchanged. Direct pushes still work, so a branch that automation writes to directly keeps working exactly as it does today. This closes the only failure a scheduled session cannot undo - rewritten or deleted history.

pr-gate._summary: history-guard, plus: a change reaches this branch only as a pull request. No human approval is required (requiredApprovals 0), so obot-merge merges exactly as it does now - the rule closes the direct-push hole, not the merge lane. Required checks are CI contexts that run on every pull request targeting this branch.

review-gate._summary: pr-gate, plus one approving review. NOT RECOMMENDED and not used by any entry below: obotclaw[bot] cannot approve its own pull request, so this converts every merge into a manual one and double-gates the carve-out - @jwildfire would attest on the PR and then approve it again in the UI. Defined here so the option is visible rather than folklore.

neverSet._note: Switches that would break the standard lane, and why each is pinned false in every tier. The verifier checks these are OFF as strictly as it checks the guards are ON - a protection that stops the agents is a failure of this spec, not a stricter version of it.
neverSet.requiredApprovals >= 1: obotclaw[bot] cannot approve its own PR; every standard-lane merge would need @jwildfire.
neverSet.requireLinearHistory: obot-merge's default strategy is a merge commit (--merge); linear history refuses it.
neverSet.strictChecks: 'require branches to be up to date' forces a rebase whenever the base moves - an unattended session would stall on it.
neverSet.requireConversationResolution: one unresolved review comment blocks the merge with nobody awake to resolve it.
neverSet.lockBranch: makes the branch read-only to everyone.
neverSet.enforceAdmins: left false on purpose so @jwildfire keeps a hand-operable override on every branch. He is the one person these rules are not defending against.
